label: Resilient Well-Connected Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They appear to be psychologically well-adjusted, with UCLA-8 loneliness scores well below typical thresholds, near-minimal PHQ-9 depression scores, and GAD-7 anxiety scores approaching zero. The combination suggests a stable, emotionally resilient group with strong social connectedness.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/social media use
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness, indicating robust social connections and sense of belonging
Exhibits near-floor depressive symptom levels on the PHQ-9
Displays virtually negligible anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7
Maintains moderate and controlled screen or social media use (1–3 hours daily)
Holds advanced educational attainment, suggesting structured daily routines and goal orientation
tone: Calm, stable, and socially engaged with an overall positive emotional baseline

label: High-Distress Digitally Immersed Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean 1.67), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean 1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean 2.16) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. With 179 respondents in this cluster, the profile represents a substantial subgroup characterized by compounded mental health challenges alongside heavy digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Higher depressive symptom severity suggesting frequent low mood, fatigue, or loss of interest
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most pronounced distress indicator in this profile
Extended daily screen time exceeding 5 hours, potentially reflecting both occupational demands and coping behaviors
Co-occurrence of all three distress dimensions, indicating a compounded psychological burden
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of multiple elevated distress indicators in a highly educated, digitally engaged population

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging approximately 1.23, PHQ-9 depression scores around 0.82, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near 0.80, these individuals fall well below clinical thresholds across all three psychological distress measures, indicating generally robust mental well-being.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, spending 1–3 hours of daily screen/online time
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of social isolation or loneliness
Demonstrates low anxiety levels well below clinical concern
Maintains moderate and bounded daily screen time (1–3 hours)
Belongs to a relatively large and stable cluster (n=341), suggesting this is a common well-being pattern among educated males
